title: Stock Futures Surge as Market Dips, Nvidia Woes Spark Live CNBC Updates
body:
U.S. equity futures nudged higher on Thursday evening after the nation’s major stock indexes slipped in regular trading, a movement largely driven by a sharp sell‑off in Nvidia shares after the unexpected departure of founder‑CEO Jensen Huang amid a brewing corporate scandal. The Dow‑related futures rose about 0.2%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq‑100 futures each added roughly 0.3%, suggesting investors were seeking a modest rebound despite lingering uncertainty surrounding the chipmaker’s leadership turmoil.

The decline in the underlying indexes was pronounced. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.5%, the S&P 500 slipped 0.7%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 1.1% by the close. Nvidia, which has been the engine behind much of the Nasdaq’s recent rally, tumbled more than 6% after the company announced Huang’s resignation, citing “personal reasons” while a separate investigation into alleged accounting irregularities and insider‑trading concerns continues to unfold. The stock’s plunge erased roughly $200 billion in market value, underscoring how central the semiconductor giant has become to broader market sentiment.

Analysts attribute the futures’ modest upside to a classic “buy the dip” mentality among institutional investors who view the broader market’s weakness as a temporary correction rather than a systemic shift. “The market is trying to separate the Nvidia story from the rest of the economy,” said Maria Torres, senior equity strategist at CapitalWave. “While the chip sector is under pressure, the underlying macro fundamentals—steady consumer spending, resilient corporate earnings, and a still‑tight labor market—remain supportive.” This sentiment was reflected in the modest gains of other technology and industrial stocks, which managed to offset some of the losses stemming from Nvidia’s volatility.

The fallout from Huang’s exit also revived concerns about governance standards in high‑growth tech firms. Nvidia, which surged more than 200% over the past 12 months, has been under scrutiny for its aggressive accounting practices and rapid expansion into artificial‑intelligence hardware. The Securities and Exchange Commission confirmed it is reviewing the company’s disclosures, while the Department of Justice has opened a parallel inquiry into possible insider‑trading activity linked to the leadership change. Investors are now weighing the risk that further regulatory actions could hamper Nvidia’s ability to capitalize on the AI boom, potentially dampening the sector’s broader momentum.

Meanwhile, the broader market is contending with a mixed backdrop of macroeconomic data. Recent consumer price index numbers showed inflation cooling to 3.2% year‑over‑year, reinforcing expectations that the Federal Reserve may pause its rate‑hiking cycle. However, a modest slowdown in manufacturing activity and a slight uptick in unemployment claims have kept some analysts cautious about the near‑term growth trajectory. The interplay of these factors created a “wait‑and‑see” atmosphere on Wall Street, where traders are balancing the positive signals from easing inflation against the negative shock from one of the market’s marquee stocks.

Looking ahead, market participants will be watching several key catalysts. First, Nvidia is slated to release its quarterly earnings in early May, a report that could either reassure investors about the company’s resilience or deepen concerns if the scandal’s fallout proves material. Second, the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting on 22 May will likely set the tone for monetary policy, with any hints of a rate hike or cut influencing risk appetite across asset classes. Finally, the resolution of the regulatory investigations into Nvidia will be a decisive factor in determining whether the chipmaker can regain its footing and whether the broader technology sector can sustain its recent rally. In the meantime, the modest rise in futures suggests that, despite the turbulence, investors remain cautiously optimistic that the market can absorb the shock and continue its upward trajectory.
